skip_reason: On the question's own terms (two or more added screens over ONE cable), no FOPO product we link makes the top three. FOPO's driver-free duals need one video link per screen: for the S11, our without-drivers page records from FOPO that 'one USB-C cable for both is not supported', and the S7 is recorded the same way. The S788 runs its three screens through FOPO's UsbDisplay driver and ships with an external PD power supply, so it is not one cable either. The KYY X90E (Windows), the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 (Windows natively, Mac with an adapter) and the Duex Max DS (one added screen) hold the top three. One caveat: I could not read the FOPO S10's connection text (fopomonitor.com returned HTTP 429 on every product read and fopodisplay.com returned 403). The S10 is the only FOPO dual that could still change this.
gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, according to the maker or reviewer, no two-screen extender on a MacBook runs both added screens over one cable without an adapter or driver: Xebec's compatibility table says every Mac, whatever its port, needs the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter (only Windows/Linux/ChromeOS ports with DisplayPort or Thunderbolt 3+ work with no adapter), and TechRadar found the one-cable KYY X90E works only on Windows. On a Mac, the one-cable, driver-free answer is a single added screen.
standout_why: Compared against TechRadar's KYY X90E review (cited), the two Mobile Pixels product pages (cited), theofficejournal.com's USB-C extender guide and itechguides.com's 2025 guide. TechRadar says the X90E 'won't work with Apple MacBook systems' but says nothing about other two-screen units. theofficejournal never mentions Mac mirroring, MST or the base-M-chip limit. itechguides only warns that 'one USB-C cable does not mean one cable will work with every laptop'. Neither guide mentions FOPO. None of these pages gives Xebec's port-by-OS table or says that Macs need an adapter for any one-cable dual. ChatGPT's answer only said 'verify compatibility' for the Xebec. Our own pages (results 2 and 3) carry the Trio 3 Pro driver rule, the FOPO one-link-per-screen rule and ViewSonic's MST quote, but not the Xebec table or the KYY Windows-only finding.
decides: It splits the pick by operating system. On a Windows laptop with DP Alt Mode or Thunderbolt, two added screens over one cable are possible with no driver: the KYY X90E per TechRadar, and the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 per Xebec's table. On a MacBook, one cable and no driver means one added screen (Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS). For two screens on a Mac you need Xebec's Mac Adapter, or the Trio 3 Pro with Mobile Pixels' driver and a power adapter, or two cables. FOPO's driver-free duals need one video link per screen, so they fail the 'one cable' condition for two screens. That is why I'm returning skip.
